punchline: A girl who read at three grew up to ask the question that gives a book its title.
thirty_sec: Oprah Winfrey was born in 1954 in Kosciusko, Mississippi, and spent her first six years with her grandmother Hattie Mae Lee, who taught her to read before age three. At six she moved to Milwaukee, and by 1962 she was staying for a time with her father in Nashville.
question: Who taught you something very early on, and when did you last tell anyone that part of your story?
key_contrast: A life holds both the people who helped and the events that hurt.
